Ancient solar eclipses may rewrite Egyptian history. An eclipse in 2471 B.C. could explain Pharaoh Shepseskaf's tomb choice. item.title: Tiny egg-eating snake discovered in Ethiopia
item.description:
【AI 精简版】 AI-condensed version. This text was produced by an LLM from the original article and may omit details. The original link at the end is the only authoritative source.

Biologists found new egg-eating snake species in Ethiopia's Bale Mountains. The white-throated egg-eater (Dasypeltis albigularis) was recently described. These snakes eat only shelled embryos, have a unique saw-like backbone for shell opening, and are small, less than 8 inches long. The species is found in Africa and the southwest corner of the Arabian peninsula.

Source: Popular Science | Published: 2026-11-20 17:01 UTC

Original link: https://www.popsci.com/environment/egg-eating-snake-discovered-ethiopia/
